'''Charles Hallam Brenner''' is an American mathematician who is the originator of forensic mathematics.
His father [[Joel Lee Brenner]] was a professor of mathematics and his mother Frances Hallam Brenner was a city councilor and briefly mayor of [[Palo Alto, California]]. His uncle [[Charles Brenner (psychiatrist)|Charles Brenner, MD]] was a psychiatrist.

Brenner received a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] from Stanford University in 1967, and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) in 1984.<ref name=PhD /><ref>{{cite journal|last=Brenner|first=Charles H.|date=November 1986|title=Asymptotic Analogs of the Rogers-Ramanujan Identities in Number Theory|journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A|volume=43|issue=2|doi=10.1016/0097-3165(86)90069-5|pages=303–319|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Brenner participated in the implementation of [[APL (programming language)|APL\360]] and APL\1130,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Breed|first=Lawrence M.|author-link=Lawrence M. Breed|date=August 2006|title=How We Got To APL\1130|journal=Vector, Journal of the British APL Association|volume=22|issue=3|url=https://archive.vector.org.uk/art10001190|access-date=3 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160318185611/http://archive.vector.org.uk/art10001190|archive-date=18 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>
and implemented the transpose and rotate primitive functions.<ref>{{cite journal|last=McDonnell|first=Eugene E.|author-link=Eugene McDonnell|date=September 2000|title=DNA Analysis in APL|journal=Vector, Journal of the British APL Association|volume=17|issue=3|url=https://archive.vector.org.uk/art10005630|access-date=3 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160419032858/http://archive.vector.org.uk/art10005630|archive-date=19 April 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

More recently, Brenner specializes in the use of mathematics in DNA analysis.<ref name=nytimes>{{cite journal|last=Dreifus |first=Claudia|author-link=Claudia Dreifus|date=8 August 2000|title=A Math Sleuth Whose Secret Weapon Is Statistics|journal=New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/08/08/science/conversatipon-with-charles-brenner-math-sleuth-whose-secret-weapon-statistics.html?pagewanted=all|access-date=3 April 2016}}</ref> His principal areas of interest and achievement in the mathematics of forensic DNA are kinship, rare [[haplotype]] matching, and DNA mixtures. In a couple of Y haplotype papers, most recently,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Brenner|first=Charles H.|date=January 2014|title=Understanding Y Haplotype Matching Probability|journal=Forensic Science International: Genetics|volume=8|issue=1|url=https://dna-view.com/downloads/documents/Understanding%20Y%20haplotype%20matching%20probability.pdf|access-date=3 April 2016|doi=10.1016/j.fsigen.2013.10.007|pages=233–243|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307174703/http://www.dna-view.com/downloads/documents/Understanding%20Y%20haplotype%20matching%20probability.pdf|archive-date=7 March 2016|url-status=dead|pmid=24315614}}</ref> he showed why Y haplotypes must be much rarer, and how much rarer, than their sample frequency in a reference population sample. Brenner’s Symbolic Kinship Program,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Brenner|first=Charles H.|date=February 1997|title=Symbolic Kinship Program|journal=Genetics|volume=145|issue=2|pages=535–42|doi=10.1093/genetics/145.2.535 |url=https://www.genetics.org/content/genetics/145/2/535.full.pdf|access-date=3 April 2016|pmid=9071605|pmc=1207816}}</ref> which can for example assess the identification evidence based on DNA profiles from an anonymous body and an arbitrary set of presumed relatives, has been widely used in mass victim identification projects, including identifying about 1/3 of the identified [[World Trade Center (1973–2001)#Destruction|World Trade Center]] bodies.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Smith|first=Matt|date=6 March 2002|title=Truth Over Death|journal=SF Weekly|url=https://www.sfweekly.com/sanfrancisco/truth-over-death/Content?oid=2144273&showFullText=true|access-date=6 April 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Whitfield|first=John|date=23 April 2003|title=World Trade Centre Forensics Break New Ground|journal=Nature|url=https://www.nature.com/news/2003/030421/full/news030421-2.html|access-date=3 April 2016|doi=10.1038/news030421-2|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Brenner played a key role in the resolution of the [[Larry Hillblom#Paternity controversy|Larry Hillblom inheritance case]], resulting in four Amerasian children each receiving $50 million.<ref>{{cite news|last=Smith|first=Matt|date=5 April 2000|title=Ca$h for Genes|journal=SF Weekly|url=https://www.sfweekly.com/sanfrancisco/cah-for-genes/Content?oid=2138346&showFullText=true|access-date=5 April 2016}}</ref>

==Anecdotes==
* Between 1968 and 1973, Brenner lived in London, U.K. and supported himself by playing [[contract bridge]] professionally.<ref name=nytimes /><ref>{{citation|last=Brenner|first=Charles H.|title=Bridge Player 1968-1973 London|url=https://dna-view.com/bridge.htm|access-date=6 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315035020/http://dna-view.com/bridge.htm|archive-date=15 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Brenner asked Gordon, his advisor, “How far can you get in mathematics without being smart?”<br>“Quite far,” he said.<ref>{{citation|last=Brenner|first=Charles H.|date=3 February 1999|title=The Realm of Mathematics|url=https://dna-view.com/math.htm#realm|access-date=6 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315005007/http://dna-view.com/math.htm#realm|archive-date=15 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>
